newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Second body recovered after Singapore tanker fire.
newsitem.headline: Second body recovered after Singapore tanker fire.

text.p: The body of a second Chinese seaman has been recovered from an oil tanker that caught fire in Singapore harbour on Wednesday, an official from the owners said on Friday.
"We found the body this morning and everyone's been accounted for," the official from Ocean Tanker Pte Ltd said.
The body of one crewman was found earlier after the blaze aboard the 26,909-dwt Singapore-registered Ocean Trader, while two men are in hospital with extensive burns. All four victims were Chinese.
The tanker was berthed at an oil terminal operated by U.S. oil company Mobil Corp when it caught fire on Wednesday evening.
Mobil said the tanker was discharging condensate, a type of light crude oil, to the Mobil refinery when the accident occurred. The cause of the blaze is not known.
"We are waiting for the green light to discharge the cargo," the Ocean Tanker official said.
The offshore terminal is joined by a pipeline network to Mobil's 300,000 barrel per day refinery on mainland Singapore.
A Mobil spokeswoman said earlier that the fire on the Ocean Trader would not affect refinery operations. The Mobil refinery is the second largest in Singapore, Asia's main refining centre.
